about: Manifest seal cases (SPEC §4, #573): each manifest's verdict over its own three hashes. Both the Rust reader (tessera-core tests/seal_cases.rs) and the reference reader (run.py) must reach every verdict, so they agree by construction. 'ok' = verifies, 'tampered' = a hash mismatch, 'refused' = not read (not I-JSON: a duplicate key, NaN, an out-of-range number, a lone surrogate; or an unsupported major tessera_version; or a block name listed twice, SPEC §5, #734; or a value in a spelling SPEC §4 doesn't define, #873: the manifest, its producer, generation or a blocks/sources/ingest_transform entry as anything but an object, such as a JSON array, or a block kind as anything but a string, such as {"array": null}); a missing seal is 'tampered'. Every case is otherwise well-typed per SPEC §5: a reader that also checks scalar field types refuses more, which these cases don't test. newer_fields = what the Rust view reports as not interpreted. Built from corpus/files by resealing with reader.manifest_seal.
